# ci-compute-github spec

The `spec` block on this engine's entry in `forge-ci.yaml`.

| Key | Type | Required | Means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | string | yes | The owner/name the workflows, secrets and runs live on. |
| `dir` | string | no | The repo checkout directory relative to the pipeline root. Defaults to the repo basename. |
| `apiBaseURL` | string | no | The GitHub API base. Defaults to the public API; tests point it at a fake. |
| `tokenEnv` | string | no | The environment variable holding the API token for the run tool. Defaults to GITHUB_TOKEN. |
| `ref` | string | no | The branch dispatches target and pushes land on. Defaults to main. |
| `setup` | list | no | Setup actions run first in every command workflow and the runner, each {uses, with}. The instance names its own toolchain actions; this engine renders whatever it is handed. |
| `workspace` | object | no | The checkout preamble every command workflow and the runner share: bootstrapCommand (one verbatim command that stands the whole workspace up in the working directory, naming its own factory) and toolchainScript (verbatim install block). Required once any command workflow or the runner exists. bootstrapCommand is always required; toolchainScript only when spec.container is unset, because an image supplies the toolchain instead. What the script installs is cached by a caches entry keyed by repos. |
| `container` | object | no | The image every job that builds a workspace runs inside, so its tools arrive prebuilt and no install step is rendered: {ref: <image reference, tag included>} typed here, or {file: <path under the pipeline root>} naming the file a workspace sync generates from its resolved toolchain pin - the resolver owns the version and this engine only reads it at declare time, so a register-advanced pin reaches the rendered workflows on the next reconcile with nobody editing a pipeline file. Exactly one of ref or file. It replaces the toolchain install and not the checkout: an image carries tools, not members, so bootstrapCommand still runs. A fan-out job never takes one - it builds no workspace. Absent runs on the runner itself, which is what a factory that PUBLISHES an image needs: a pipeline running inside the image it builds could not publish a fixed one after a bad release. |
| `runsOn` | string | no | The runner label every rendered job runs on. Defaults to ubuntu-latest. |
| `concurrency` | object | no | The group every command workflow serializes its runs on: {group, cancelInProgress}. Defaults to the platform's own name for the workflow, queued rather than cancelled - an apply that is writing state must finish, and the next one then sees what it wrote; one push wave dispatches once per member, and concurrent applies race the state repo. |
| `caches` | list | no | What every workspace-building job restores before its bootstrap and saves afterwards, each {name, paths, key}. key content (the default) names the saved cache by a listing of what it holds and restores the newest for this OS, which is right for a store that converges on its own; key repos hashes the heads of the pipeline's repos, exact match only, and is restored after the checkout and saved after the toolchain script, which is right for a toolchain built from the checkout - a run of several jobs installs it once. Absent means one cache, the tool store under ~/.cache/forge keyed by content, which is what every job carried before the key existed; an empty list means no cache. A repos key on a pipeline that declares no repos is refused. |
| `carry` | object | no | How what a job built crosses to the jobs after it: {compression: gzip|none, retention: <days>}. Defaults to gzip and 7. Binaries compress and the upload is billed by the byte; an image layout is blobs that are already gzip and spends a minute compressing nothing, so a factory carrying one says none. |
| `failureReport` | object | no | The issue a failing run of a workflow with reportFailure opens: {title, body}. {{.Workflow}} in the title stands for the workflow's name. Defaults to "<workflow> is failing" and a body naming the run. |
| `actions` | object | no | The platform actions the rendered steps use, pinned: {cache, downloadArtifact, uploadArtifact}. Defaults to actions/cache@v6, actions/download-artifact@v8 and actions/upload-artifact@v7. |
| `secrets` | list | no | The Actions secrets to seal, each with name and the fromEnv variable its value is read from (default GITHUB_TOKEN). |
| `workflows` | list | no | The owned workflows, each a kind with its parameters or verbatim content, plus an optional header comment block. A command workflow starts on its on block - {cron, events, push: {branches, ignorePaths}}, written quoted as "on": because a YAML 1.1 parser reads a bare on as the boolean true - where a cron or a dispatch event always takes workflow_dispatch as well, push also starts it on a push to this repo (how a factory pipeline reruns when its own workspace files change) and ignorePaths keeps a push touching only those paths from starting it at all (the platform's own filter, blind to what a file is for, so list only what nothing embeds). A command workflow also takes reportFailure (open an issue when a run fails - set it on a workflow nobody watches, meaning a cron run or a repository_dispatch somebody fired from another repo). Every command workflow serializes its own runs on spec.concurrency, and every workspace-building job restores and saves spec.caches. A release workflow needs a secret too, because it stands the workspace up to reach the toolchain and that clone reaches private members. |
| `jobs` | string | no | How a command workflow is cut. whole (the default) renders one job running the whole apply. stage renders one job per phase - self-reconcile, evaluate - then one per pipeline stage, its substages running beside each other inside it, each job running one phase of the apply with --phase, so the run reads as what it is instead of one job named after its first step. substage renders one job per substage instead, so a failure shows exactly where it happened, at the cost of one workspace checkout per job. Cut into phases: there is no release job, because a release is a substage naming an artifact engine; the self-reconcile job answers one word, superseded or converged, and the evaluate job runs only on converged, so the run the settle's push fired is the one that carries the work; the evaluate job answers skip or proceed and reports the revision this run proves, every job after it runs only on proceed and is handed --revision, so a run with nothing to release shows them skipped and a run whose own stages move one of the pipeline's repos still answers for the commits it started with. A stage job keeps what IT built as an Actions artifact - never what it inherited - and a job in any later stage brings back every one this run has written, or exactly the ones its substages declared with uses. Neither cut renders a job for a stage's promotion: the jobs that need to know whether the stage in front advanced ask the promotion themselves. Every job is titled from the stage and substage names unless the pipeline declares a displayName. A stage named self-reconcile or evaluate is refused. |
| `runner` | object | no | The run tool's dispatch target: name, secret, setupScript (verbatim block before the targets), pollIntervalSeconds, timeoutMinutes. Without a name the engine cannot run substages. |

forge-ci never validates a spec. This engine does, because only it knows what the keys mean.
